hero.intro: The numbers below come from a crawl of dmp.com on 13 September 2026, a Semrush pull on the domain and its competitors, nine buyer searches run live from Springfield, Missouri, and six questions put to Claude with web search from the same city. This is the baseline we measure against at 30, 60 and 90 days.

hero.heading: Where dmp.com stands, and what it is worth to fix

findings.fix: Build one Springfield, Missouri page at /springfield-missouri/ covering the headquarters, the product lines and the local dealer list, titled for the city and the state so the engines stop confusing it with the other Springfields. In the build.
findings.cost: Every buyer, specifier and installer searching security in Springfield lands on a competitor or on a page about Springfield Illinois, Ohio or Tennessee. DMP is headquartered in the city and is not in the conversation for a set of terms whose difficulty scores are 0 and 1.
findings.title: DMP does not appear in the top ten for a single buyer search asked from its own city
findings.evidence: Nine searches were run from Springfield, Missouri and dmp.com is absent from all nine top-ten lists. barcomsecurity.com holds position 1 for 'commercial security system springfield' and appears in five of the nine, passfireandsecurity.com in five, centralillinoissecurity.com in five, safehome.org in six and vivint.com in five. The terms that carry demand are small but easy: 'commercial security system springfield' is 90 a month at difficulty 1, 'video surveillance system springfield' 90 a month at difficulty 0, 'access control system springfield' 20 a month at difficulty 0, 'alarm monitoring springfield' 10 a month at difficulty 0. The other four have no Semrush entry, which puts them under about 10 a month.

findings.fix: The fix is the same body of work that fixes the search results: a Springfield page, seven named service pages and Organization schema on the home page so the engine has something to read and attribute. In the build, then measured again at 30 and 90 days.
findings.cost: When someone asks an assistant who supplies intrusion, access control or monitoring in Springfield, the answer is assembled from other companies' pages and from directories DMP has no profile on. That is a channel where the brand simply does not exist.
findings.title: Named in none of the AI answers about security in Springfield
findings.evidence: Six questions were put to Claude with web search from Springfield, Missouri on 13 September 2026. Four returned an answer and two timed out. DMP was named in 0 and cited in 0. The sources the engine read instead were barcomsecurity.com in three answers, expertise.com in three, and atlassecurity.com, georgealarm.com, securitymonster.com, springfieldalarmcompany.com and vivint.com in two each.

findings.fix: Serve a 301 from dmp.com to the canonical host, publish robots.txt and an XML sitemap at both hosts, and put a self-referencing canonical on the home page. In the build, week one.
findings.cost: Every tool, partner and answer engine that starts at dmp.com rather than www.dmp.com gets a redirect and no map of the site. It also means the eight AI crawlers are allowed only because there is no file saying otherwise, not because anyone decided it.
findings.title: The apex domain answers with a 307 and carries no robots.txt and no sitemap
findings.evidence: A crawl starting at https://dmp.com/ found exactly 1 URL. It returned HTTP 307, 2 words of body text, an empty title, no H1, no canonical, no internal links and no structured data. No robots.txt was readable and no XML sitemap was found at that host. Semrush shows the www host ranking for 7,462 keywords, so the catalogue is indexed, but nothing at the apex tells a crawler or an audit tool where to go.

findings.fix: Add Organization plus LocalBusiness schema to the home page with the Springfield address, a tappable phone number and sameAs links to the company's LinkedIn, YouTube, Facebook and Crunchbase profiles, and add Product schema to the control panel, keypad and access control template. In the build.
findings.cost: Search engines and answer engines have no confirmed statement of who DMP is, where it is or what it makes, so they fall back on third-party pages such as Indeed, Glassdoor and Reddit. A manufacturer with a product catalogue is also publishing no Product markup, so its panels and keypads cannot be surfaced as products.
findings.title: The company is not described as an entity anywhere a machine can read it
findings.evidence: The page the crawler could read carries no structured data at all: 0 Organization, 0 LocalBusiness, 0 Product, 0 BreadcrumbList, 0 FAQPage, and 0 sameAs links to any profile. There is no machine-readable address and no tappable phone number. vivint.com's Springfield page carries Organization, Service, PostalAddress, GeoCoordinates and ContactPoint; safehome.org's carries Organization, LocalBusiness, PostalAddress, ItemList and BreadcrumbList.

findings.fix: Build the seven service line pages and a resource hub that target category language rather than part numbers, starting with access control and fire. In the build for the pages, 90-day plan for the content programme.
findings.cost: The site harvests existing dealers and customers looking up model numbers and support logins. It does not introduce DMP to anyone who has not already heard the name, so the whole top of the funnel depends on trade shows, reps and word of mouth.
findings.title: Two thirds of the traffic is people who already know the brand
findings.evidence: Semrush puts branded share at 66 percent. The top organic term is 'dmp' at 9,900 a month, holding 32.33 percent of all traffic on its own, followed by 'digital monitoring products' at 880 and a long list of part numbers: 'dmp xr150' 390, 'dmp keypad' 390, 'dmp xr550' 260, 'dmp 734' 210. The one high-volume non-branded term in the top thirty is 'white on white paper' at 12,100 a month, position 9, which lands on the JamAlert white paper and has nothing to do with security.

findings.fix: Build a page for each of the seven lines at /intrusion-alarm-systems/, /access-control-systems/, /fire-alarm-systems/, /video-surveillance/, /alarm-monitoring/, /wireless-security-systems/ and /commercial-security-systems/, each with Service schema, question headings and links down to the relevant SKUs. In the build.
findings.cost: A buyer who searches 'access control systems' (9,900 a month) or 'fire detection and fire alarm system' (6,600 a month) meets a part number page written for someone who already chose the part. Those searches go to distributors and integrators instead.
findings.title: Seven product and service lines have no page of their own that we could find
findings.evidence: The seven lines on record, intrusion alarm systems, access control systems, fire alarm systems, video surveillance, alarm monitoring and communicators, wireless security systems and commercial security systems, have no page path recorded and none was reachable from the apex crawl. The answer-shaped content component scores 0 of 100 and the on-page fundamentals component 8 of 100. Semrush shows the top-ranking pages are all individual SKUs such as /products/control-panels/xr-series/xr150 and /products/access-control/modules/734.

findings.fix: Publish an about and proof page carrying dealer testimonials, installation case studies and Review markup, and link it from the home page and every service page. In the 30-day plan.
findings.cost: Anyone checking DMP out before specifying it, and any AI answer summarising the brand, reads employment complaints first because the company publishes nothing that answers the question. No Review or AggregateRating markup exists anywhere on the site to compete.
findings.title: The brand reputation result is owned by job boards and Reddit
findings.evidence: The search 'digital monitoring products reviews', run from Springfield, returns indeed.com at 1, glassdoor.com at 2 and a r/springfieldMO thread at 3 titled 'I can't recommend anyone work for DMP'. Positions 4 to 10 are simplyhired.com, a second glassdoor.com result, facebook.com, a second indeed.com result, ipvm.com, mammothsecurity.com and securityinfowatch.com. dmp.com appears nowhere on the page.

findings.fix: Put six to eight questions with direct answers and FAQPage markup at the foot of each of the seven service pages, drawn from the question lists above. In the build for the markup, 30-day plan for the copy.
findings.cost: These are exactly the phrasings answer engines lift from. Because nobody in this set has claimed them, the ground is open and DMP is choosing not to stand on it.
findings.title: Nothing on the site answers a question in the words buyers use
findings.evidence: The crawl found 0 question headings and 0 FAQPage markup on the money page, and no blog or insights section. Semrush records real question demand across the lines: 'how to turn off fire alarm system' 720 a month, 'how to reset fire alarm system' 320, 'what is access control system' 210, 'what is fire alarm system' 210, 'what is the best home video surveillance system' 210, 'what is a central station fire alarm system' 170. None of the four Springfield competitors carries FAQPage markup either.

findings.fix: Put a tappable phone number, the Springfield address and a short 'find a dealer' form on the home page and repeat them on all seven service pages and the Springfield page. In the build.
findings.cost: A dealer or specifier who does reach dmp.com has to go looking for a route to a human. Every step between interest and contact loses a share of the people on it.
findings.title: The page that should take the enquiry offers no way to make one
findings.evidence: The home page has no form, no tel link, no readable address and no contact vendor script. The demand capture component scores 1 of 100 and money page readiness averages 4 of 100 across the one money page measured. vivint.com, safehome.org and centralillinoissecurity.com all carry a form on their Springfield pages; barcomsecurity.com carries a phone number.

findings.fix: Point the access control and fire pages at the difficulty 22 to 42 commercial terms and build supporting question pages beneath them. In the 90-day plan.
findings.cost: There is no pipeline of non-branded demand at all, and the winnable commercial terms are being left to distributors while the unwinnable consumer terms are quoted as the target.
findings.title: The category head terms are all unranked, and the reachable ones are being ignored
findings.evidence: DMP holds no position for any of the ten highest-volume terms in its categories: 'security camera' 550,000 a month, 'adt' 246,000, 'diy home security systems' 135,000, 'best home security cameras' 110,000, 'home security systems' 74,000. Semrush values reaching position 3 on that set at 173,873 clicks a month and $1,063,192 a month in paid equivalent. Those are consumer terms at difficulty 46 to 79 and the outlook on every one is long haul, but the commercial terms are within reach of an Authority Score of 39: 'access control systems' 9,900 at difficulty 58, 'fire detection and fire alarm system' 6,600 at 42, 'smart smoke detector' 6,600 at 35, 'access control companies' 1,600 at 29, 'door access control systems' 1,600 at 22.

findings.fix: Earn links from domains that have none yet, starting with security trade publications, the Springfield chamber and business press, and dealer sites, and ask partners who link with a logo to put the company name in the alt text. In the 90-day plan.
findings.cost: The headline link number overstates the real position. If that one relationship or that one site changes, most of the profile goes with it, and image links say nothing about what DMP makes, so they build no topical signal.
findings.title: The backlink total rests on one relationship
findings.evidence: The profile is 22,880 links from 1,916 referring domains, above the median of 832 across the five competitors measured, and 88.1 percent of the links pass authority. But nationaljeweler.com accounts for 85.3 percent of every link to the site, and 89.7 percent of links, 20,514 of 22,880, are image links carrying no anchor text. Authority Score is 39 against 60 at vivint.com and 55 at safehome.org.

findings.fix: Publish a deliberate robots.txt that names and allows the eight crawlers, and an llms.txt listing the home page, the seven service pages, the Springfield page and the support hub. In the build, week one.
findings.cost: Low today, but the moment anyone adds a default robots.txt the access can disappear without being noticed, and there is no file telling an engine which pages matter.
findings.title: AI crawlers are allowed by accident, not by policy, and llms.txt is not published
findings.evidence: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, Bingbot and Googlebot are all able to read the site, which scores 94 of 100 on AI answer access against 100 at safehome.org. That permission exists because no robots.txt was readable, not because a file grants it. llms.txt is not published.

findings.fix: Once the service pages exist, run a small brand-defence campaign on the five brand terms and a test on 'access control companies' and 'door access control systems'. In the 90-day plan.
findings.cost: Nothing is being wasted, but nothing is being defended either. With 'dmp' at 9,900 a month and rising dealer interest, a competitor or a distributor can bid on the brand name at any time and pay very little for it.
findings.title: No paid search at all, and no paid-sourced contacts in the CRM
findings.evidence: DMP runs 0 ad keywords. HubSpot records 0 contacts from paid search, 0 from paid social and 0 from display in the 90 days since 15 June 2026. vivint.com buys ten of its own brand terms, including 'vivint' at 165,000 a month and $8.05 a click and 'vivint security' at 22,200 a month and $11.90 a click.

compare.intro: Each column was parsed the same way on 13 September 2026: the client's money page at dmp.com, and for each competitor the exact page that ranked in the Springfield searches.
compare.verdict: Barcom wins the Springfield results with 1,078 words, a phone number and almost no markup, which shows how low the bar is in this market. Vivint and SafeHome win the wider category with a named city page, a form and a full entity description in schema. Copy Barcom's city page structure and Vivint's markup, and take the FAQ ground that none of the four has claimed.

moves.body: A crawl starting at https://dmp.com/ found one URL that returned HTTP 307 with 2 words, no title, no H1 and no canonical, and neither robots.txt nor an XML sitemap was readable there. Serve a permanent redirect from the apex to the canonical host, publish robots.txt and an XML sitemap at both hosts, and add a self-referencing canonical to the home page. Name the eight AI crawlers in the new robots.txt so their access is a decision rather than an accident, and publish llms.txt alongside it. This is the cheapest fix in the report and every other measurement depends on it.

The one readable page has no H2 sections and no question headings, so there is not a single answer-shaped block anywhere the crawler reached.

The question demand is real and unclaimed: "how to turn off fire alarm system" at 720 a month, "do it yourself wireless home security systems" at 320, "what is access control system" at 210, "what is the best home video surveillance system" at 210, and "how does access control system work" at 70.

That means there is nothing on the site written in the language a buyer or an AI engine uses when it asks how a system works, what it costs or which type to choose. do: Serve the home page at one canonical host with a 200 response, a title and a single H1 that both name Digital Monitoring Products, Springfield, Missouri and the category.

Add Organization and LocalBusiness JSON-LD to the home page with the legal name, the Springfield address, the phone number, the logo and sameAs links to LinkedIn, Crunchbase, BBB, YouTube and Grokipedia.

found: Organization schema, LocalBusiness schema and Review schema are all absent from the home page, and the structured data component scored 0 of 100.
There are no sameAs links, so nothing on dmp.com connects the company to its LinkedIn, Crunchbase, BBB or Grokipedia entries, all of which already link back to the site.
No address a search engine can read and no tappable phone number were found anywhere on the site, and there are no location pages.
The home page has no title, no meta description and no H1, so even the plainest name signal is missing.

Authority is not the problem: 1,916 referring domains with an Authority Score of 39, above the median of 832 domains across the five measured competitors. The company is well linked and badly described.
entity.intro: An answer engine decides what a company is from structured data on its home page and from the profiles that data points to. DMP publishes none of it. The home page returned a 307 and carried no schema of any kind, no address, no phone number and no sameAs links, so every machine reading the site has to guess. That is why the brand result is filled by job boards and why Claude named other companies instead.

entity.heading: Nothing on dmp.com tells a machine who Digital Monitoring Products is

today: Semrush shows dmp.com with 7,462 organic keywords and 24,493 organic visits a month, valued at 247,680 a month in equivalent paid traffic, and zero paid keywords running.
66 per cent of that organic traffic comes from people already searching the brand: "dmp" alone at 9,900 a month accounts for 32.33 per cent of it.
The home page returned a 307 and, as read on 13 September 2026, had an empty title, an empty H1, two words of copy, no canonical tag, no Open Graph image and no internal links.
The crawler could reach exactly one URL on the site, because there is no robots.txt at dmp.com/robots.txt and no XML sitemap to follow.

The pages that earn the visits are product and support pages: the home page takes 49.01 per cent of organic traffic across 209 keywords, the dealer admin page 3.52 per cent, the 734 access module page 2.93 per cent and the control panels index 2.63 per cent.
The single money page, the home page, scored 4 of 100 in the page audit: no form, no tappable phone number, no FAQ, no city in the title and no schema.
Asked nine buyer searches from Springfield, Missouri, DMP appeared in the top ten for none of them.

Backlinks are strong on paper, 22,880 links from 1,916 domains at Authority Score 39, but 85.3 per cent of the links come from a single domain, nationaljeweler.com, and 89.7 per cent are image links carrying no anchor text.

aeo.intro: On 13 September 2026 we asked Claude with web search six buyer questions about security in Springfield, the same six that map to DMP's service lines. Four returned an answer and two timed out; DMP was named in none of them and cited in none of them, while barcomsecurity.com and expertise.com were read in three answers each.

backlinks.heading: 1,916 domains of authority, and 85 per cent of the links come from one site

local: The query "digital monitoring products reviews", asked from Springfield, Missouri, returns no dmp.com page in the top ten.
Indeed holds first place with "Working at Digital Monitoring Products, Inc.: 25 Reviews", an employer review page, not a product one.
Glassdoor holds second place and appears twice in the top ten with employer reviews.
A Reddit thread in r/springfieldMO sits third, titled "I can't recommend anyone work for DMP".
SimplyHired, Facebook and a second Indeed listing take four more of the ten places.
The only industry results are ipvm.com, mammothsecurity.com and securityinfowatch.com, none of them owned or influenced by DMP.
No star rating appears in any result title except Indeed's count of 25 reviews, and no review markup was found on dmp.com, so no rating can be shown next to the brand in search.

Across the eight service and buyer queries asked from Springfield, Missouri, DMP is absent from all top tens; the ten places are held by passfireandsecurity.com, barcomsecurity.com, centralillinoissecurity.com, eccoinc.com, safehome.org, vivint.com, springfieldalarmcompany.com and others.
plan: Fix the front door. Replace the 307 on the apex with a single 301 to one canonical host, publish robots.txt and an XML sitemap covering every product, support and resource URL, add a self-referencing canonical tag, and give the home page a title, a meta description, one H1 and Organization plus LocalBusiness schema with the Springfield address and phone number.

Build the seven service line pages: intrusion alarm systems, access control systems, fire alarm systems, video surveillance, alarm monitoring and communicators, wireless security systems and commercial security systems. Each gets 800 words or more, H2 sections, a FAQ block marked up as FAQPage using the pulled questions, Service schema, ten or more internal links and an enquiry form.

Build the Springfield, Missouri page with the city in the title, the address, a tappable phone number, a form and links to the seven service pages, and add sameAs links from the home page schema to LinkedIn, Crunchbase, BBB, YouTube and Grokipedia.

Take back the brand result: publish an about page, a careers page and a company news page under dmp.com so branded queries have owned destinations, start collecting first-party reviews, and publish the first three answer posts against the access control, fire alarm and video surveillance questions.

Re-run the same nine Springfield searches, the same six AI questions and the same page audit against this baseline, and decide whether to open a small paid search test on the reachable access control terms rather than the 543,664 a month the full national list would cost.

hub.heading: Where you stand in search today, and what changes
hub.intro: Measured before we touched anything, so the work can be judged against it.
today: Semrush shows dmp.com with 7,462 organic keywords and 24,493 organic visits a month, valued at 247,680 a month in equivalent paid traffic, and zero paid keywords running.
66 per cent of that organic traffic comes from people already searching the brand: "dmp" alone at 9,900 a month accounts for 32.33 per cent of it.
The home page returned a 307 and, as read on 13 September 2026, had an empty title, an empty H1, two words of copy, no canonical tag, no Open Graph image and no internal links.
The crawler could reach exactly one URL on the site, because there is no robots.txt at dmp.com/robots.txt and no XML sitemap to follow.

The pages that earn the visits are product and support pages: the home page takes 49.01 per cent of organic traffic across 209 keywords, the dealer admin page 3.52 per cent, the 734 access module page 2.93 per cent and the control panels index 2.63 per cent.
after: Every URL answers once, at one canonical host, with a robots.txt and a sitemap.
Eight product line pages, each with a FAQ marked up as FAQPage and Service schema.
A Springfield, Missouri page with the address, phone and a form.
Organization and LocalBusiness schema on the home page, with sameAs links.
An about page, a careers page and a news section the brand search can land on.
keep: Product pages that already earn traffic keep their address or get a 301
hub.note: Rankings and traffic depend on the market and on what you publish after launch. What we promise is that nothing about the build is the reason they do not come, that every number is re-measured at 30, 60 and 90 days, and that you see the same report we do.
